introduction: This spec defines the data-model construction and rendering logic that enables the night-shift fix pipeline to build afspec `Spec` objects in memory from `TriageResult` output, giving night-shift coders the same structured context format (EARS requirements, test contracts, task groups) produced by the `code` command.

glossary.AcceptanceCriterion: A single criterion inside a TriageResult, with fields: id, description, preconditions, expected, and assertion.
glossary.InMemorySpec: A wrapper type in agentfox.nightshift.spec_builder that holds a fully constructed afspec Spec object without any on-disk representation.
glossary.NS-REQ: The requirement ID prefix used for night-shift in-memory requirements (e.g. NS-REQ-1).
glossary.PRDDocument: The afspec Pydantic model representing the product requirements document metadata and body attached to a Spec.
glossary.PRDFrontmatter: The metadata section of a PRDDocument, containing spec_id and spec_name fields.
glossary.Requirement: A single afspec requirement entry with id, title, user_story, acceptance_criteria, and edge_cases fields.
glossary.Requirements: The afspec Pydantic model that holds a list of Requirement objects.
glossary.Spec: The top-level afspec Pydantic model that aggregates Requirements, TestSpec, Tasks, and a PRDDocument into a single structured object.
glossary.Subtask: An individual work item within a TaskGroup, with id, title, details, state, test_spec_refs, and requirement_refs fields.
glossary.SubtaskState: An enum used to track the current state of a Subtask (e.g. PENDING, DONE).
glossary.TS-NS: The test case ID prefix used for night-shift in-memory test cases (e.g. TS-NS-1).
glossary.TaskGroup: A group of Subtask objects under a shared kind and title within the afspec Tasks model.
glossary.Tasks: The afspec Pydantic model that holds a list of TaskGroup objects.
glossary.TestCase: A single afspec test case with id, requirement_id, description, preconditions, expected, assertion_pseudocode, input, and kind fields.
glossary.TestSpec: The afspec Pydantic model that holds a list of TestCase objects.
glossary.TriageResult: The output object produced by the night-shift triage agent, containing a list of AcceptanceCriterion objects derived from a GitHub issue.
glossary._render_spec_sections: The existing disk-based rendering function in session/context.py that loads a Spec from disk and produces markdown sections.
glossary.afspec: The internal Python library providing Pydantic models (Spec, Requirements, TestSpec, Tasks, etc.) and rendering utilities for structured specifications.
glossary.assemble_context: The function in session/context.py that aggregates rendered spec sections and other context for the coder's system prompt.
glossary.build_afspec_from_triage: The adapter function defined in nightshift/spec_builder.py that converts a TriageResult into an in-memory afspec Spec.
glossary.build_system_prompt: The function that takes assembled context and constructs the final system prompt string injected into the coder agent.
glossary.fix-{issue_number}: The spec_id pattern used for ephemeral night-shift specs (e.g. fix-42).
glossary.issue_number: The numeric identifier of the GitHub issue being fixed in a night-shift session.
glossary.render_individual: The afspec library function that accepts an in-memory Spec object and returns rendered markdown sections.
glossary.render_inmemory_spec_sections: The extracted rendering function in session/context.py that converts an in-memory Spec to markdown section strings.
glossary.requirements: The afspec JSON artifact containing EARS-patterned requirements.
glossary.prd: Product requirements document (prd.md with YAML frontmatter).
glossary.tasks: The afspec JSON artifact containing task groups and subtasks.
glossary.test_spec: The afspec JSON artifact containing test contracts.
glossary.Requirement.id: The unique identifier field of an afspec Requirement (e.g. NS-REQ-1).
glossary.AcceptanceCriterion.id: The unique identifier field of a triage AcceptanceCriterion (e.g. AC-1).
glossary.AcceptanceCriterion.description: The description field of a triage AcceptanceCriterion.
glossary.Requirement.title: The title field of an afspec Requirement.
glossary.Requirement.user_story: The user_story field of an afspec Requirement.
glossary.AcceptanceCriterion.preconditions: The preconditions field of a triage AcceptanceCriterion.
glossary.AcceptanceCriterion.expected: The expected outcome field of a triage AcceptanceCriterion.
glossary.Requirement.acceptance_criteria: The acceptance_criteria list field of an afspec Requirement.
glossary.Requirement.edge_cases: The edge_cases list field of an afspec Requirement.
glossary.TestCase.id: The unique identifier field of an afspec TestCase (e.g. TS-NS-1).
glossary.TestCase.requirement_id: The requirement_id field linking an afspec TestCase to its Requirement.
glossary.NS-REQ-{N}: The ID pattern for night-shift requirements where N is a sequential number.
glossary.AcceptanceCriterion.assertion: The assertion field of a triage AcceptanceCriterion.
glossary.TestCase.description: The description field of an afspec TestCase.
glossary.TestCase.preconditions: The preconditions field of an afspec TestCase.
glossary.TestCase.expected: The expected outcome field of an afspec TestCase.
glossary.TestCase.assertion_pseudocode: The assertion_pseudocode field of an afspec TestCase.
glossary.TestCase.input: The input field of an afspec TestCase (empty string when not applicable).
glossary.TestCase.kind: The kind field of an afspec TestCase (e.g. acceptance).
glossary.SubtaskState.PENDING: The PENDING variant of the SubtaskState enum, indicating a subtask has not started.
glossary.TS-NS-{N}: The ID pattern for night-shift test cases where N is a sequential number.
glossary.render_individual(spec): The afspec function that renders a Spec into per-artifact markdown strings.
glossary.afspec.save(): The afspec function that persists a Spec to disk (not used in this spec).
glossary.afspec.load_spec(): The afspec function that loads a Spec from a disk directory (not used in this spec).
glossary.render_inmemory_spec_sections(spec): The new public function that renders an in-memory Spec to markdown sections.

user_story.goal: call build_afspec_from_triage(triage_result, issue_number) and receive a fully populated in-memory afspec Spec
user_story.benefit: the coder agent receives the same structured EARS requirements, test contracts, and task groups that the code command produces from on-disk specs

acceptance_criteria.action: return an afspec `Spec` object whose `requirements`, `test_spec`, `tasks`, and `prd` fields are all populated from the provided `TriageResult` and `issue_number`
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: afspec Spec instance (in-memory, no file I/O performed)

acceptance_criteria.action: perform no file system reads or writes, no calls to afspec.load_spec() or afspec.save(), and no disk I/O of any kind
be importable from agentfox.nightshift.spec_builder and have the signature build_afspec_from_triage(triage_result: TriageResult, issue_number: int) -> Spec

edge_cases.action: return a `Spec` with empty `Requirements` and `TestSpec` collections and a single `TaskGroup` containing one `Subtask` titled "Fix the issue"
edge_cases.return_contract: Spec instance with empty requirements and test_spec; tasks contains exactly one TaskGroup with one Subtask

edge_cases.action: substitute an empty string for that field rather than raising an exception
edge_cases.return_contract: Spec instance constructed successfully with empty-string defaults for missing fields
edge_cases.error_condition: any field of an `AcceptanceCriterion` (description, preconditions, expected, assertion) is None or empty string

user_story.goal: have each AcceptanceCriterion translated into a correctly mapped afspec Requirement
user_story.benefit: the coder sees EARS-structured requirements that mirror exactly the triage findings

acceptance_criteria.action: map each `AcceptanceCriterion.id` (e.g. "AC-1") to a `Requirement.id` using the pattern "NS-REQ-{N}" where N is the 1-based index of the criterion
set `Requirement.title` to `AcceptanceCriterion.description`
set `Requirement.user_story` to the criterion description verbatim, without any template or LLM call
set `Requirement.acceptance_criteria` to a list containing exactly one entry derived from `AcceptanceCriterion.preconditions` and `AcceptanceCriterion.expected`
set `Requirement.edge_cases` to an empty list for every mapped criterion

user_story.goal: have each AcceptanceCriterion produce a corresponding TestCase in the afspec TestSpec
user_story.benefit: the coder receives actionable test contracts without a separate test-generation step

acceptance_criteria.action: map each `AcceptanceCriterion` to exactly one `TestCase` in `TestSpec`
set `TestCase.id` using the pattern "TS-NS-{N}" where N matches the 1-based criterion index
set `TestCase.requirement_id` to the corresponding `NS-REQ-{N}` identifier for the same criterion

set `TestCase.description` to `AcceptanceCriterion.description`, `TestCase.preconditions` to `AcceptanceCriterion.preconditions`, `TestCase.expected` to `AcceptanceCriterion.expected`, and `TestCase.assertion_pseudocode` to `AcceptanceCriterion.assertion`
set `TestCase.input` to empty string and `TestCase.kind` to the string "acceptance" for every derived test case

user_story.goal: have build_afspec_from_triage produce a single TaskGroup with one Subtask per criterion
user_story.benefit: the coder sees a flat, actionable task list aligned with the issue being fixed

acceptance_criteria.action: create exactly one `TaskGroup` with id=1, kind="tests", and title="Fix issue #{issue_number}"

create one `Subtask` per `AcceptanceCriterion` with id "1.N" (1-based sequential), title equal to the criterion description, details list containing preconditions, expected, and assertion, state set to `SubtaskState.PENDING`, test_spec_refs referencing the corresponding `TS-NS-{N}` id, and requirement_refs referencing the corresponding `NS-REQ-{N}` id

edge_cases.action: create a single `TaskGroup` containing one `Subtask` with title "Fix the issue", empty details, state `SubtaskState.PENDING`, and no test_spec_refs or requirement_refs

user_story.goal: have a minimal PRDDocument attached to the in-memory Spec
user_story.benefit: rendering functions that expect a complete Spec structure receive valid metadata without requiring persisted spec files

acceptance_criteria.action: construct a `PRDDocument` with `PRDFrontmatter` where spec_id="fix-{issue_number}" and spec_name="fix_issue_{issue_number}", and body equal to the sanitized issue body text from the `TriageResult`
leave optional PRDDocument fields (status, created_at, owner, etc.) at their Pydantic defaults — do not populate them

user_story.goal: call render_inmemory_spec_sections(spec) and receive the same markdown section list that _render_spec_sections() produces for on-disk specs
user_story.benefit: night-shift coders receive identically formatted structured context without code duplication between the disk-based and in-memory paths

acceptance_criteria.action: accept a single `Spec` argument and return a list of markdown section strings by delegating to `render_individual(spec)`
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: list[str] — one string per rendered markdown section (## Requirements, ## Test Specification, ## Tasks)

acceptance_criteria.action: perform no file system reads or writes during rendering
be refactored to call `render_inmemory_spec_sections` internally after loading the `Spec` from disk, eliminating duplicated rendering logic

edge_cases.action: propagate the exception to the caller without swallowing or wrapping it
edge_cases.error_condition: `render_individual` raises an exception for any reason

requirements.title: ID consistency between Requirements, TestSpec, and Tasks

user_story.goal: have all cross-references between Requirement ids, TestCase ids, and Subtask refs use consistent NS-REQ-{N} and TS-NS-{N} patterns
user_story.benefit: rendering and downstream tooling can reliably cross-reference requirements, tests, and tasks

acceptance_criteria.action: ensure that for every criterion at index N, the Requirement id "NS-REQ-{N}", the TestCase id "TS-NS-{N}", and the Subtask id "1.N" all refer to the same source AcceptanceCriterion
set each Subtask's test_spec_refs to ["TS-NS-{N}"] and requirement_refs to ["NS-REQ-{N}"] for its corresponding criterion index N

correctness_properties.title: Criterion count equals Requirement count equals TestCase count
correctness_properties.invariant: the returned `Spec` has exactly N `Requirement` objects in `Requirements`, exactly N `TestCase` objects in `TestSpec`, and exactly N `Subtask` objects in the single `TaskGroup`

correctness_properties.title: Cross-reference consistency across all IDs
correctness_properties.for_any: criterion at 1-based index N in a TriageResult
correctness_properties.invariant: Requirement.id == "NS-REQ-{N}", TestCase.id == "TS-NS-{N}", TestCase.requirement_id == "NS-REQ-{N}", Subtask.id == "1.N", Subtask.test_spec_refs == ["TS-NS-{N}"], and Subtask.requirement_refs == ["NS-REQ-{N}"]

correctness_properties.title: No file I/O performed during Spec construction or rendering
correctness_properties.invariant: no file system reads or writes occur; no calls to `afspec.load_spec()` or `afspec.save()` are made

correctness_properties.title: render_inmemory_spec_sections output is identical to _render_spec_sections for the same Spec
correctness_properties.for_any: any `Spec` object loaded from disk by `_render_spec_sections`
correctness_properties.invariant: the markdown section list returned by `render_inmemory_spec_sections(spec)` is equal to the list that `_render_spec_sections` returned for that same spec before refactoring

steps.action: calls build_afspec_from_triage(triage_result, issue_number) with a TriageResult containing one or more AcceptanceCriterion objects
iterates over criteria, constructing NS-REQ-{N} Requirement objects, TS-NS-{N} TestCase objects, and 1.N Subtask objects, then assembles a Spec with PRDDocument
returns the fully populated in-memory Spec to the caller without touching the file system
calls render_individual(spec) and returns a list of markdown section strings (## Requirements, ## Test Specification, ## Tasks)
injects the returned markdown sections into the coder's system prompt via build_system_prompt
calls build_afspec_from_triage(triage_result, issue_number) where triage_result has an empty criteria list
detects empty criteria list and constructs a Spec with empty Requirements and TestSpec, and a single TaskGroup with one Subtask titled "Fix the issue"
returns the fallback Spec to the caller
passes the fallback Spec to render_inmemory_spec_sections(spec), which returns minimal markdown sections for the coder prompt

execution_paths.title: Disk-based rendering refactored to reuse render_inmemory_spec_sections

steps.action: triggers _render_spec_sections() to render a spec loaded from disk
loads the Spec from disk via afspec.load_spec() and then delegates rendering to render_inmemory_spec_sections(spec)
calls render_individual(spec) and returns the markdown section list
returns the markdown sections to assemble_context, producing identical output to the pre-refactor behavior

error_handling.behavior: Return a Spec with empty Requirements and TestSpec and a single TaskGroup containing one Subtask titled "Fix the issue" with SubtaskState.PENDING

error_handling.condition: Any AcceptanceCriterion field (description, preconditions, expected, assertion) is None or empty string
error_handling.behavior: Substitute an empty string for the missing field value and continue constructing the Spec without raising an exception

error_handling.condition: render_individual raises an exception during render_inmemory_spec_sections
error_handling.behavior: Propagate the exception to the caller as-is without swallowing or wrapping it
